A.label: ORIGINAL_CPU_TGS_BASELINE
A.single_dimension: Original scene, CPU SimulationContext, TGS, authored native drives; no force writes; no strict fd=dq rejection.

B.label: TGS_SETTINGS_AND_DRIVES
B.single_dimension: Same original CPU baseline plus exact installed solver attributes, iteration counts, gravity, drive gains/targets and effort modes.

C.label: NON_BASELINE_EXTERNAL_FORCES_EVERY_TGS_ITERATION
C.single_dimension: Temporary anonymous stage only: set installed PhysxSceneAPI EnableExternalForcesEveryIteration=True before SimulationContext; never call it original frozen configuration.

D.label: GPU_BACKEND_DIAGNOSTIC
D.single_dimension: Temporary backend diagnostic only if actual host supports CUDA; record effective backend/scene differences; not equivalent original-scene evidence.

E.label: ORIGINAL_MOTION_SETTLE
E.single_dimension: Original CPU TGS startup motion followed through bounded window; compare moving and settle samples without replacing dq.

F.label: SOURCE_FAULT_CONTROL
F.single_dimension: Pure deterministic source/actuation fault controls; no Isaac scene or command writes.

hypothesis_tests.no_auto_validity: TGS explanation alone does not qualify a torque-control source.
hypothesis_tests.primary: TGS end-of-step velocity can differ from whole-step displacement velocity under drives/gravity/constraints.
supporting_signals: moving link/joint response has signed reproducible transitions
PGS/GPU differences are labeled backend diagnostics

settled_state: actual displacement and internal dq separately recorded
solver_semantics: end-step dq explicitly treated as solver velocity, not average velocity

scene_policy: original builder only; no saved scene/USD/fixture/bridge/ACM/historical evidence modifications
torque_policy: If source/dynamics are not qualified, no effort write is allowed; latch rejection and report skipped cells.
